1) How SCIM groups map into Redwood IAM roles (we'll have dozens of AD groups mapped to fine-grained roles).

If so, what are the field names/expected values and the provisioning cadence (delta vs full).

Also flagging two compliance questions from our security team: certificate rotation window for SAML signing, and whether SCIM provisioning will include 'external_id' or a stable identifier we can use for reconciliation.

Hi Laura — thanks for the context and the attachments. Short answers up front: yes, we support group->role mappings via SCIM and we also accept SAML group assertions for on-the-fly role assignment. We typically recommend using a combination of both: SCIM for authoritative group membership and SAML for session-time claims.

Couple of immediate notes:
- SCIM: we support incremental (delta) provisioning and full-sync, and we include externalId and an immutable id on each user and group object for reconciliation.
- SAML: our control plane accepts group claims in either 'groups' or 'memberOf' attributes; for role mapping use the claim 'redwood_roles' or map groups to role strings in the dashboard.
- Cert rotation: we recommend a 90-day rotation window for signing certs to meet most enterprise policies; short-lived (30d) is also supported if you automate re-uploads.

I've looped in Ben (runtime/integration lead) and Dev (ops) to scope the runbook and meet. Proposed slots: Tue 2028-06-06 09:00-10:00 PDT or Wed 2028-06-07 14:00-15:00 PDT. Which works for you?

Laura — few more technical details to help your IdP/SCIM team:

1) SCIM schema we return: user.id (immutable), user.externalId (your AD GUID), user.userName (email), group.id, group.displayName, group.externalId. We patch groups/users with incremental changes (we send 304-style responses on no-changes).

2) Group->Role mapping: in Private Control Plane you can define mapping rules: e.g. if group.displayName startsWith 'rwd-admin-' -> role:admin; you can use exact match or regex match. The mapping table is exportable as CSV for audit.

3) SAML: prefer a multi-valued attribute 'redwood_groups' (URI or name). If using Okta, the recommended transform is to add a Group Push integration (Okta SCIM) for authoritative membership and set the SAML app to emit 'redwood_roles' which are strings like 'infra:read,infra:write,model:serve'. If you want scoped claims (tenant-level) we support namespaced roles like 'org:acme:role:devops'.

4) Reconciliation: include group.externalId from your AD as externalId on SCIM. That makes lookups O(1) and avoids rename issues.

5) Rate limits: SCIM writes limit of 200 req/min for Private CP control plane endpoints by default; we can raise for Dedicated customers or during initial sync windows.

I'll prepare a minimal runbook (curl examples, Okta screenshots) and upload it before the call.

—Ben

Quick ops note from my side:
- Service account for SCIM: we ask customers to create a long-lived service account in their IdP with a scoped role for group read+push. We'll also accept a short-lived OAuth client from your IDP if you prefer token rotation.
- SAML cert rotation: Redwood supports metadata URL fetch and manual cert upload. If you host metadata at a stable URL we can auto-fetch and alert 14 days before cert expiry.
- Audit logs: every SCIM modification is recorded in the control plane audit trail (who, when, delta). We can stream logs to your SIEM via syslog/forwarder if needed.

I'll include the ops-runbook section in the doc Ben mentioned.

—Dev
